name: WY at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: Wyoming's R+23 partisan lean in an open seat held by Republicans
Huge resource gap: Gray raised $1.6M plus outside support vs. $18K for the Democrat
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~98%
No polling or expert ratings, but fundamentals uniformly favor Republicans
model.rationale: Wyoming's R+23 baseline, a well-funded Republican nominee against a barely funded Democrat, and markets at 98% Republican all point to a safe Republican hold; the open seat adds no offsetting factor. I shade the margin slightly beyond the baseline given the lopsided money and uncontested dynamics of the environment.
model.watch: A major scandal or third-party (Constitution/Libertarian) surge splitting the right could tighten the margin, though not the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Harriet Hageman (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Wyoming's at-large House seat is among the most Republican-leaning in the country, with a partisan lean of R+23. Harriet Hageman is leaving the seat to run for Senate, but the Republican nominee, Chuck Gray, enters the general election with roughly $1.6 million raised and nearly $900,000 in outside support. Democrat Lisa Kinney has raised under $20,000, with minimal cash on hand and no outside backing.

There are no public polls or expert ratings for this race, and prediction markets give the Republican about a 98% chance of winning. The quantitative baseline puts the expected Republican margin near 19 points; the resource imbalance and open-seat dynamics justify a somewhat wider expected margin. Barring an extraordinary development, this seat will remain in Republican hands.
